before.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\frac{}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

after.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\frac{}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(AA∂x−Q∂gA+R)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
−P, ∂g, ∂y
b
−P, ∂g, ∂x
c
P, ∂g, ∂y
d
P, ∂g, ∂x
e
−P, ∂P, ∂x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

content.knowledge_point: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula
content.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\frac{}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{z}⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le x.$
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+y)=1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+y)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{z}⟩{|}_{z=x+y} \\  & =⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{x+y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{{xy}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{x+y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{{e}^{x+y}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨xy,\,x+y,\,{e}^{z}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(xy)\cdot 1-(x+y)\cdot 1+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-xy-x-y+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}(-xy-x-y+{e}^{x+y})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}-xy-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{x+y}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-{x}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{2x}-{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{2x}-{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2x}}{2}-{e}^{x}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-e)-(0+\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{2}-8e-1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $x=k(y,z)$ for $(y,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(P-\,-R\,)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $x=k(y,z),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(y,z)=⟨k(y,z),\,y,\,z⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂k}{∂z},\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂k}{∂y} & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{∂k}{∂z} & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨1,\,-\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,-\frac{∂k}{∂z}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,-\frac{∂k}{∂z}⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(P-Q\,\frac{∂k}{∂y}-R\,\frac{∂k}{∂z})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

For a surface S given by x=k(y,z) for (y,z)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(P−AA−RA)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
−Q, ∂k∂x, ∂k∂z
b
−Q, ∂k∂y, ∂k∂z
c
−Q, ∂k∂z, ∂k∂y
d
Q, ∂k∂y, ∂k∂z
e
Q, ∂k∂y, ∂k∂x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form x=k(y,z), it can be parameterized as

r(y,z)=⟨k(y,z),y,z⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ry′=⟨∂k∂y,1,0⟩rz′=⟨∂k∂z,0,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ry′×rz′=|ijk∂k∂y10∂k∂z01|=⟨1,−∂k∂y,−∂k∂z⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(ry′×rz′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨1,−∂k∂y,−∂k∂z⟩dA=∬D(P−Q∂k∂y−R∂k∂z)dA.

content.knowledge_point: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula
content.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $x=k(y,z)$ for $(y,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(P-\,-R\,)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $x=k(y,z),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(y,z)=⟨k(y,z),\,y,\,z⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂k}{∂z},\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂k}{∂y} & 1 & 0 \\ \frac{∂k}{∂z} & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨1,\,-\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,-\frac{∂k}{∂z}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-\frac{∂k}{∂y},\,-\frac{∂k}{∂z}⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(P-Q\,\frac{∂k}{∂y}-R\,\frac{∂k}{∂z})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩,

decision.explanation: Using the activity's upward orientation, g_x=√(y/x) and g_y=√(x/y). The flux integrand is −Pg_x−Qg_y+R=−1−x/y+4xy+1=x(4y−1/y). Hence the flux is (∫₃⁴x dx)(∫₁²(4y−1/y) dy)=(7/2)(6−ln 2), which is option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=2\sqrt{xy}$ for $3\le x\le 4$ and $1\le y\le 2.$
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩{|}_{z=2\sqrt{xy}} \\  & =⟨{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{4xy+1}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1-\frac{x}{y}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{[-x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+2x{y}^{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+8x+0-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2){[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{7(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=2\sqrt{xy}$ for $3\le x\le 4$ and $1\le y\le 2.$
content.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩{|}_{z=2\sqrt{xy}} \\  & =⟨{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{4xy+1}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1-\frac{x}{y}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{[-x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+2x{y}^{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+8x+0-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2){[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{7(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=2x+y$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
after.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x+y)=2 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x+y)=1\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨3{x}^{3}y,\,2yz,\,2x(y+z)⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨3{x}^{3}y,\,2yz,\,2xz⟩{|}_{z=2x+y} \\ F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨3{x}^{3}y,\,2y(2x+y),\,2x(y+2x+y)⟩{|}_{z=2x+y} \\  & =⟨{{3{x}^{3}y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{4xy+2{y}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{4xy+4{x}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
